newsitem.title: CHINA: China premier says Britain unrealistic on HK.
newsitem.headline: China premier says Britain unrealistic on HK.

text.p: Chinese Premier Li Peng said on Friday that it was unrealistic for Britain to expect to monitor Beijing's compliance with the Sino-British accord on the return of Hong Kong.
"Recently, someone from the British side said he would monitor the implementation of the joint declaration on Hong Kong," Li told reporters.
"I think this is unrealistic. After July 1, Hong Kong's sovereignty returns to China," he said.
"It will be entirely China's internal affair."
The British colony reverts to Chinese rule on July 1 under a 1984 Sino-British accord that calls for Beijing to grant the territory a high degree of autonomy for 50 years.
British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind has said Britain would monitor events in Hong Kong after the transfer of power and report to parliament every six months.
Beijing has already come under sharp criticism from Hong Kong, Britain and the United States for its plans to dismantle the territory's elected legislature and replace it with an appointed body.
It also has come under attack from civil rights activists in Hong Kong for its plans to amend or repeal many of the territory's existing civil liberties laws.

The U.S. House of Representatives approved a bill declaring that China's plans to abolish the Hong Kong legislature would violate the Sino-British accord, and called on Beijing to live up to its obligations under the agreement.
China has lashed out at the U.S. Congress, saying this was gross interference in its internal affairs.
The Chinese premier also repeated Beijing's pledge not to interfere in Hong Kong's affairs after the handover.
